methodologyNote: claude plugin eval is still early-access gated in this environment. These numbers come from manually adopting each agent's role file in a fresh proxy agent and running the eval case's prompt.md by hand — real tool use, real repo state, graded manually against each case's graders/*.md. Not the native harness's aggregate-result.json. Full methodology and caveats in docs/COST-BASELINE.md.

costMethodology.note: Token totals are unsplit (input+output+cache combined) — no per-run breakdown is available from a manually-spawned agent's completion summary. costUsd below uses a blended rate assuming ~88% input / 12% output tokens, typical for a tool-heavy agentic loop (mostly file reads and tool results, comparatively little generated text) — an estimate, not a measurement. costUsdRange gives the true bounds: costUsdRange[0] if every token were input-priced, costUsdRange[1] if every token were output-priced. Re-derive from response.usage once the native claude plugin eval harness is available.

history.note: Baseline — first dry run of each of the 8 cases that existed at the time.

Validates the new ask-before-shipping requirement: 3 regressions (one repeat of a Round 1 case, two cases run for the first time) plus 2 ad-hoc checks — not yet permanent eval files — confirming the new behavior actually fires on a genuinely ambiguous work item / test oracle.

comparablePair.note: The only case run identically in both rounds — same fixture, same grader. Every other row above differs between rounds, so this is the sole apples-to-apples data point. n=1 vs n=1 — not a real median, reported honestly rather than treated as proof either way.

findings.summary: 3 ambiguities in run-plan/SKILL.md and plan-verifier.md (unattended-run approval, "installed" meaning, untracked-file evidence) — shipped in 1.0.1
implementer, test-writer, doc-writer, and plan-verifier now stop and ask on a genuinely ambiguous work item instead of guessing — shipped in 1.0.2, validated by 5 additional dry runs
spec-creator called Bash for a state-changing mkdir before Write, violating its own read-only-Bash constraint — now covered by a permanent grader
eval fixtures shared an unnamespaced file path and raced when run concurrently — fixed, but the fix itself has not yet been exercised by a real run
